summary: Initial residency and audit evidence discovery. Hightide evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PII/HIPAA-like and financial-data use. Primary concerns: log retention and redaction, key residency (KMS/HSM), SOC2/ISO evidence, tenant isolation, and fallback behavior during capacity events. Redwood AE+SE outlined hosting options, control plane boundaries, and audit artifacts available. Agreed next steps: share docs and schedule technical deep dive.

Is there an on-prem package we can run behind our VPC?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04 11:00 AM ET
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Benji Ortiz (Redwood SE), John Lema (CISO, Hightide), Priya Nair (Head of AI), Evan Brooks (Infra Lead), Sana Patel (Legal), Mark Ruiz (Product)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro from us - I'm Alex, AE on the account, Maya is our SE who will handle the technical details, Benji will chime on perf. Could you go around real quick?
[00:08] John (CISO): John here, CISO at Hightide. We're looking at LLM for internal risk workflows and some customer-facing summarization. Primary constraints are auditability and residency.
[00:15] Priya (Head of AI): Priya, Head of AI. We own the models and the prompt pipelines. We want to know if we can keep full control of keys and logs.
[00:21] Evan (Infra): Evan, infra lead. Questions about network topology, VPC peering, and whether logs hit our environment.
[00:28] Sana (Legal): Sana from legal — mainly interested in evidence for regulatory audits and data retention controls.

[00:35] Maya (SE): Great, thanks. High level: Redwood offers three modes — Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). I'll sketch the control plane boundaries and what artifacts each mode produces.
[00:46] Priya: Quick thing — we have workloads that are HIPAA-adjacent for a subset of customers and GDPR where PII can't leave EU. Any nuance there?
[00:55] Maya: Yep. Hosted can be region-restricted — we can pin requests to eu-west regions. However, with hosted some control plane metadata (billing, monitoring) remains in our control plane — we can provide audit logs but not all raw request payloads by default unless you opt for dedicated or private.
[01:12] John: When you say "audit logs", what exactly? We need timestamped request logs, redaction markers, who accessed which keys, and an indelible trail for auditors.
[01:22] Maya: We produce request/response metadata, latency, token counts, and an index of which model and route processed the request. For hosted we store full transcripts for a configurable retention window. We also offer a sanitized log pipeline — you can choose to zero out or hash prompt text at ingress.
[01:40] Evan: How does that redaction work? Is it client-side or server-side? And is it reversible?
[01:47] Maya: There are two levers. We can enable client-side redaction (best practice) where your app strips PII before calling Redwood. Server-side redaction is offered as a built-in pipeline — it replaces matched PII patterns with tokens and those matches are not reversible by default. We also support a hybrid where you send encrypted payloads and we perform computation inside a private tenant if you go with Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[02:12] Priya: Important — we need KMS/HSM keys to never leave our control. Can you integrate with our cloud KMS or an HSM in our VPC?
[02:20] Maya: Yes. Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration. Private (VPC) can be configured to use your KMS endpoints so keys remain in your account. For hosted there are customer-managed key options but the control plane still needs to perform some orchestration; we document what cryptographic material stays with you.
[02:37] Sana: For SOC2 audits, we need evidence. What can you hand us?
[02:42] Alex (AE): We'll share our SOC2 Type II report, and Maya will follow up with a list of specific artifacts we can provide per deployment mode — e.g., access logs, key rotation history, RBAC changes, and network peering configs.
[02:53] John: Does "access logs" include raw prompt text? For compliance we need a copy for a subset of tracked transactions for up to seven years in some regs.
[03:02] Maya: For hosted, we can retain raw transcripts but that's a commercial and privacy decision — we can configure retention windows and export raw logs on request. For Dedicated and Private it's typical to keep raw logs in your account or your S3 bucket, depending on setup. If you need seven-year retention we will need to design an archival path — we can push logs to your long-term archive (encrypted S3) under your control.
[03:22] Mark (Product): If we export to S3, is there any chance Redwood will ever read those logs?
[03:27] Maya: If the bucket and credentials are owned by you and we use direct delivery (push), Redwood doesn't have access. In some hosted setups we store logs in our storage and can export on request; those would be accessible to our ops per our policies unless you choose dedicated/private.
[03:40] Evan: Networking — for Private, do we run any runtime inside our VPC? How heavy is the on-prem appliance?
[03:46] Benji (SE): The private package can be deployed as a managed appliance (containerized runtime) inside your VPC. It contains the inference runtime and a slim control agent. All model execution and KV cache stays in your network. Control plane interactions are minimized to telemetry and billing metadata which can be cut off for air-gapped installs. The on-prem bundle needs GPU nodes that you provide; we ship the runtime images and an ops guide.
[04:11] Priya: We need the ability to pin model versions and ensure fallback policies do not leak data outside the EU. If primary model unavailable, we cannot route to a global hosted fallback.
[04:21] Maya: Right — routing policy rules are configurable. You can set geographic-only fallbacks or fail closed. We typically recommend a fallback to a smaller open model in-region, but we can configure strict residency and failover to a hold queue instead.
[04:36] John: About tenant isolation: With Dedicated, is it physical isolation or logical? We have subsidiaries with separate legal entities and want strong separation.
[04:45] Maya: Dedicated is single-tenant GPU pools — that means compute isolation at the cluster level. Networking and storage can be isolated. Control plane still orchestrates but with clear tenancy boundaries and per-tenant encryption keys; we provide per-tenant audit trails. Private gives you maximum isolation because the control plane can be run locally.
[05:02] Sana: Legal wants to know about legal hold and e-discovery. If regulators request specific chat transcripts, can we retrieve them and provide chain-of-custody evidence?
[05:12] Maya: We can provide exportable archives with timestamps, request IDs, signer hashes of the logs, and a signed manifest. For high-assurance workflows we support WORM-like storage in your archive and external notary-stamped manifests. Some of that is part of our enterprise package.
[05:30] Evan: How about cross-region replication of logs? If we keep data in eu-west, will disaster recovery ever replicate outside?
[05:37] Maya: We don't replicate your logs outside selected regions unless you've opted in. For hosted with region pinning we keep data in-region. If you choose Dedicated in a particular region, we can configure replication only within that region or to your DR site under your control.
[05:50] Priya: A practical question — what's the latency hit if we enable server-side redaction or encryption at rest with customer keys?
[05:58] Benji: Typical overhead for server-side redaction is small ~5-15ms per request depending on regex work and throughput. KMS envelope encryption round trips can add 20-50ms if not cached. But in Dedicated/Private deployments where the KMS is in the same VPC, KMS latency is negligible. We'll share benchmark numbers tailored to your topology.
[06:20] John: We're concerned about retention windows and legal holds — if a user asks for deletion, how do we ensure complete erasure including cached KV tokens?
[06:29] Maya: Deletion flows include purging request logs and KV cache entries. For cached KV (key-value) we call it KV cache — ocasionally transcribed as "K V cache" in older docs — we ensure cache invalidation and for private deployments you can also rotate or destroy keys which renders cached ciphertext useless. We record deletion operations in an audit trail.
[06:52] Sana: And about subpoenas — will Redwood turn over customer data if served? What's the process?
[06:58] Alex: We'd respond to lawful process consistent with our agreements. For dedicated/private deployments where logs and keys are under customer control, we would notify you per our policy. For hosted, we have a legal team that follows our terms — we'll put specifics in the legal appendix.
[07:12] Mark: Competitor check — we heard MegaCloud AI offers in-region endpoints but doesn't do per-request redaction. Any differentiator?
[07:18] Maya: Our differentiator is the combination: region pinning + configurable redaction + customer-managed keys + per-tenant audit artifacts. Also control plane abstractions for consistent API across modes.
[07:31] Priya: Priya again — one subtlety: when you anonymize prompts server-side, can we still run evals that compare model quality across sanitized vs raw? We need to verify quality drop.
[07:40] Maya: We offer an eval pipeline that can run against sanitized copies if you want. Alternatively you can opt to keep internal eval buckets with raw prompts in your own archive. We'll help instrument quality checks pre/post redaction.
[07:53] John: On certifications — SOC2 yes, but do you have any attestation on subsections like logging integrity?
[07:59] Maya: The SOC2 covers availability and security controls. For logging integrity we can provide supplemental artifacts: signing manifests, key rotation history, and tamper-evidence notes. For some customers we provide a third-party auditor package under NDA.
[08:12] Evan: We have a nonfunctional requirement: <=120ms p95 for 256-token responses in production. Is that achievable with Dedicated?
[08:20] Benji: Yes, with Dedicated reserved pools in us-east we can hit that for smaller models. For large 8k-context models the p95 will be higher. We'll propose batching and KV cache settings to meet SLOs. Also show how cost scales.
[08:34] Sana: Regarding access control: we use SAML SSO and strict RBAC. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP for per-route permissions?
[08:41] Maya: Yes, SAML/SCIM integration is supported. You can map roles to API keys and limit which teams can call certain model endpoints. We also offer token-level auditing.
[08:52] Priya: If we go with Hosted for speed of rollout, and later move to Dedicated, is there a migration path for logs, keys, and pinned model versions?
[08:59] Maya: We support migration. Logs and artifacts can be exported. Keys require reconfiguration — if you used our hosted-managed keys you'd need to rotate into customer-managed keys during migration. We have runbooks and a migration plan template.
[09:12] John: One more on the legal side: e-discovery requires chain-of-custody proofs. Do you provide signed manifests with hashes?
[09:19] Maya: Yes, we can provide signed manifests and per-archive hashes. For the highest assurance we recommend Private or Dedicated with your own signing keys so you can attest independently.
[09:31] Alex: OK, maybe useful to recap. Hightide's primary concerns: PII handling and long-term retention for audit, keys never leaving your control, strict geo-residency, and robust chain-of-custody. On our side: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but requires decisions on retention and keys; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and key control; Private gives maximum isolation with on-prem runtime.
[09:54] Mark: Sounds right. Can you show a mapping of controls to deployment options? i.e., which artifacts we get on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[10:02] Maya: We'll provide a controls matrix in the follow-up doc. It will map: available logs (raw transcripts, metadata), key ownership, KMS integration, RBAC depth, legal hold capabilities, region pinning, and SLA guarantees.
[10:15] Priya: We'd like a short pilot — start with Hosted in eu-west limited to redacted transcripts and do an in-region Dedicated POC for our highest-sensitivity flows. Is that feasible?
[10:24] Alex: Absolutely, a hybrid pilot is a common path. Can we agree on next steps to make that concrete?
[10:30] John: Yes — deliverables from Redwood: pricing + SLA, SOC2 sample, KMS integration doc, controls matrix, perf numbers for eu-west with our model families. From Hightide: QPS/seq length distribution, example PII patterns, and list of stakeholders for the deep dive.
[10:46] Alex: Got it. We'll schedule the technical deep dive — Maya, Benji, and I will join.
[10:50] Maya: I'll also include a sample runbook for migration from Hosted to Dedicated and notes about fail-closed routing.
[10:55] Sana: We'll need contractual language about subpoenas and notice. Please loop legal.
[10:59] Alex: Will do. Anything else?
[11:03] Speaker 6: [inaudible] — brief confirmation.
[11:07] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts by Aug 6 and propose times for the technical deep dive.

End of transcript.
